# TASK T-000 — Repository bootstrap

**Phase:** 0 · **Size:** M · **Depends on:** — · **Plan version:** 1.1.0
**Plan references:** §0, §2.2, §7 (SR-01, SR-02, SR-03, SR-11), §8.1, §9, §11.3, §13 (T-000), Appendix F, ADR-001, ADR-006, ADR-014, ADR-016
**Repository:** https://github.com/osza-tools/osza-netmon
**Provided with this card:** `plan.md` v1.1.0 (the Owner supplies the file; do not edit it)

---

## 1. Objective
Create the project skeleton so that every later task starts from a repository that builds, enforces the lint and security rules in CI, contains the plan and the agent rules, and has the license in place. This task adds **no product behavior**.

## 2. Context
- `plan.md` is the authority. Read §0, §7, §9 and §11.3 before starting.
- Name `osza-netmon` and license GPL-3.0 are confirmed. The SPDX variant is `GPL-3.0-only` until the Owner says otherwise (plan §20, O-7).
- Decision ADR-006: one Cargo package with `lib.rs` + `main.rs`. No workspace.
- The plan forbids `unsafe`, panics from external input, and printing to stdout/stderr from code that can run while the TUI is active. These rules are enforced mechanically from the first commit.

## 3. In scope
1. **Root files:** `plan.md` (verbatim copy supplied by the Owner), `AGENTS.md` (verbatim from plan Appendix F), `README.md` stub, `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`, `rustfmt.toml` (minimal), `clippy.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `deny.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`.
2. **Cargo package** `osza-netmon`, library + binary, latest stable edition supported by the pinned toolchain.
3. **Source files:** `src/lib.rs` and `src/main.rs` only.
4. **CI:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.github/dependabot.yml`.
5. **Docs skeleton:** `docs/adr/`, `docs/reports/`, `docs/poc/`, `docs/tasks/`, each with a one-line `README.md`. Put this task card at `docs/tasks/T-000.md`.

## 4. Out of scope (do NOT do)
- Any product logic: no discovery, no registry, no networking, no TUI code, no terminal initialization.
- ADR files (T-001) and core types (T-002).
- An argument-parsing crate. `--version` and `--help` are handled with `std::env::args` only.
- Release workflow, packaging, checksums (T-405).
- Editing `plan.md`. If you find an error or ambiguity in it, write a Plan Question.
- Any dependency other than `ratatui` and `thiserror`.

## 5. Requirements

### 5.1 `Cargo.toml`
- `name = "osza-netmon"`, `description`, `repository = "https://github.com/osza-tools/osza-netmon"`, `readme`, `license = "GPL-3.0-only"`, `publish = false`.
- `rust-version` (MSRV): the lowest stable Rust that builds the full dependency tree with `--locked`; record how you determined it.
- Dependencies: `ratatui` and `thiserror` at their latest stable versions at the time of the task (plan §9.1 "Approved"). They are included now so that `cargo deny` and `cargo audit` are validated against the real dependency tree and the GPL-3.0 license allowlist early. Record the exact resolved versions.
- `[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
- `[lints.clippy]`: deny `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `indexing_slicing`, `panic`, `todo`, `dbg_macro`, `print_stdout`, `print_stderr`.
- `clippy.toml`: allow these lints inside tests (`allow-unwrap-in-tests`, `allow-expect-in-tests`, `allow-panic-in-tests`, `allow-indexing-slicing-in-tests`, `allow-print-in-tests`, `allow-dbg-in-tests`). Verify each option name against the pinned clippy version and report any that is unsupported.
- `[profile.release]`: `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip = true`, `panic = "unwind"`.

### 5.2 `rust-toolchain.toml`
Pin a specific stable toolchain version (not the floating `stable` channel). Include `rustfmt` and `clippy` components.

### 5.3 Source files
- `src/lib.rs`: begins with the SPDX header, defines `pub const APP_NAME: &str = "osza-netmon";` and `pub const DISPLAY_NAME: &str = "osza Network Monitor";` (these are the only places in code where the name appears, per ADR-001), and exposes the version from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`.
- `src/main.rs`: thin. Supports `--version` / `-V` (prints `osza-netmon <version>`, exit 0) and `--help` / `-h` (short usage text, exit 0). Any other argument prints a one-line error to stderr and exits with code 2. No panics for any argument input, including non-UTF-8 arguments. The only place where `print_stdout` / `print_stderr` may be allowed, by a narrowly scoped `#[allow]` with a comment, is this file.
- Every `.rs` file starts with `// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only`.
- Include a minimal unit/integration test for the argument handling (version, help, unknown flag, non-UTF-8 argument).

### 5.4 License
- `LICENSE` must be the **verbatim** GPL-3.0 text from https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.txt. Do not write it from memory or paraphrase it. Record the source URL and the SHA-256 of the file in the report. If you cannot fetch the text, stop and raise a blocking Plan Question; the Owner will supply it.
- `README.md` stub: product name, one-line description ("a lightweight terminal application that discovers devices on the local IPv4 network and shows what is known about them"), status **pre-release / under construction**, a link to `plan.md`, the license. It must not list features that do not exist and must not claim that all devices on a network are always visible.

### 5.5 `deny.toml`
- **Licenses:** allow only GPL-3.0-compatible licenses (for example MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Zlib, Unicode-3.0). If the real dependency tree needs another license, do not add it silently — raise a Plan Question with the crate and the license.
- **Bans:** `wildcards = "deny"`; `multiple-versions = "warn"`; deny the crates prohibited by plan §9.1: `tokio`, `async-std`, `reqwest`, `hyper`, `openssl`, `openssl-sys`, `native-tls`, `pcap`. (Report any of them that appears in the tree through a dependency.)
- **Advisories:** vulnerabilities and unmaintained crates reported as errors, unless an exception is justified in the report.
- **Sources:** `unknown-registry = "deny"`, `unknown-git = "deny"`; only crates.io allowed.

### 5.6 CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
- Triggers: `pull_request` and `push` to `main`. Use `concurrency` to cancel superseded runs.
- `permissions: contents: read` at the workflow level.
- **Every third-party action pinned to a full commit SHA**, with the human-readable tag in a trailing comment. Look the SHAs up from the actions' official repositories; do not guess.
- Use `--locked` for every Cargo command; the toolchain comes from `rust-toolchain.toml`.
- Jobs (may be combined where sensible, but each gate must be visible as its own step):
  1. `cargo fmt --check`
  2. `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
  3. `cargo test --all-features`
  4. `cargo doc --no-deps` with `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings"`
  5. `cargo audit`
  6. `cargo deny check`
  7. MSRV build check using the `rust-version` from `Cargo.toml`
  8. SPDX check: fail if any `.rs` file does not start with the SPDX header
- Tools such as `cargo-audit` and `cargo-deny` are installed with pinned versions (or through an official action pinned by SHA). State your choice and the reason in the report.
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: weekly updates for the `cargo` and `github-actions` ecosystems.

### 5.7 Process
- Work on branch `task/T-000-bootstrap`. Do not push to `main` directly. Open a pull request if you have access; otherwise deliver the branch or a patch and say so in the report.

## 6. Deliverables
All files in §3; the branch/PR; and `docs/reports/T-000/execution-01.md` written with the template in plan Appendix B.

## 7. Acceptance criteria
- [ ] From a fresh clone, `cargo build --locked` and `cargo test --locked` succeed.
- [ ] `osza-netmon --version` prints `osza-netmon <version>` and exits 0; `--help` prints usage and exits 0; an unknown flag prints one line to stderr and exits 2; a non-UTF-8 argument does not panic.
- [ ] Enforcement proof: on a **throwaway** branch (not merged) four separate commits each fail the gates — (a) an `unsafe {}` block, (b) `.unwrap()` in non-test code, (c) `println!` in `lib.rs`, (d) a `.rs` file without the SPDX header. Report the CI run links or command outputs.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo doc` (warnings denied), `cargo audit` and `cargo deny check` all pass locally and in CI on the PR.
- [ ] `deny.toml` implements §5.5, passes on the real dependency tree, and the license allowlist contains only GPL-3.0-compatible licenses.
- [ ] `LICENSE` is byte-identical to the official GPL-3.0 text (URL and SHA-256 in the report); `Cargo.toml` has `license = "GPL-3.0-only"`; every `.rs` file has the SPDX header; CI enforces it.
- [ ] Toolchain pinned; MSRV determined and recorded; exact `ratatui` and `thiserror` versions recorded; `Cargo.lock` committed.
- [ ] CI uses SHA-pinned actions with `permissions: contents: read`, and it is green on the PR.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` matches plan Appendix F; `plan.md` at the root is identical to the supplied file (checksum recorded in the report).
- [ ] The `docs/` skeleton exists; `README.md` states pre-release status and the license, and makes no capability claims.
- [ ] No `unsafe`; no `println!`/`eprintln!` outside `main.rs`; no dependencies beyond `ratatui` and `thiserror`.

## 8. Constraints
- No network access at runtime or build time beyond crates.io fetches through Cargo.
- No `unsafe`, no extra dependencies, no behavior beyond §5.3.
- Do not modify `plan.md`.
- If any requirement here conflicts with the plan or cannot be met, stop and write a Plan Question (plan §14.5); do not improvise.

## 9. Verification commands (paste results in the report)
```text
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked --all-features
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --locked
cargo audit
cargo deny check
cargo run --locked -- --version
cargo run --locked -- --help
cargo run --locked -- --bogus ; echo "exit=$?"
sha256sum plan.md LICENSE
```

## 10. Report
Submit `docs/reports/T-000/execution-01.md` using plan Appendix B. Include: the resolved versions (toolchain, MSRV, `ratatui`, `thiserror`), the CI tool-installation choice, any dependency or license exception raised, and the enforcement-proof evidence.
